questions.question: What is the function of a catalyst in a chemical reaction?
options: It slows down the reaction and is chemically changed at the end.
It speeds up the reaction and is completely used up.
It speeds up the reaction without being used up or chemically changed.
It has no effect on the speed of the reaction but changes the products.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about catalysts?
options: Any catalyst can be used to speed up any chemical reaction.
Catalysts are specific to particular reactions.
Catalysts can only be used in reactions involving gases.
A single catalyst works for all oxidation and reduction reactions.

questions.question: What do we call biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions inside living cells?
options: Polymers
Monomers
Hormones
Enzymes

questions.question: What occurs during a displacement reaction in an aqueous solution?
options: A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its salt.
A less reactive metal displaces a more reactive metal from its salt.
Two metals of equal reactivity swap places in their salt solutions.
A metal reacts with water to form a metal oxide and hydrogen gas.

questions.question: When magnesium is added to copper sulfate solution, magnesium sulfate and copper are formed. What type of reaction is this?
options: Neutralisation
Thermal decomposition
Displacement
Combustion

questions.question: Which statement best describes a metal ore?
options: A pure block of metal found deep underground.
A rock that contains a metal in a form that can be extracted.
A mixture of two or more metals melted together.
A synthetic material designed to mimic the properties of metals.

questions.question: Under what condition can carbon be used to extract a metal from its ore?
options: When the metal is more reactive than carbon.
When carbon is more reactive than the metal.
Only if the metal ore is a liquid at room temperature.
Only when the metal is extremely unreactive, like gold.

questions.question: Which of the following is a typical physical property of metals?
options: They are poor thermal conductors and very brittle.
They are soft substances that harden only when heated.
They are good electrical conductors, shiny, and malleable.
They have low melting points and easily dissolve in water.

questions.question: What happens to the soft substances used to make ceramics when they are heated?
options: They melt into a flexible, stretchy liquid.
They become hard and brittle.
They dissolve and release hydrogen gas.
They turn into polymers with low melting points.

questions.question: What is an alloy?
options: A pure metal element that has been highly polished.
A mixture of elements that includes at least one metal.
A chemical compound made of non-metals only.
A long chain of small molecules joined together.

questions.question: Why are materials combined to create a composite material?
options: To ensure the material can be easily dissolved in acid.
To produce a material that has a single, unchanged property.
To create a new material with improved properties.
To make the material react more vigorously with oxygen.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes how polymers are formed?
options: Large metal atoms are split into smaller fragments called monomers.
Small molecules called monomers join together to form very long chains.
Ceramics are heated until they form flexible crystalline structures.
Carbon reacts with metal ores to form long molecular sheets.

questions.question: What is the effect of adding a plasticiser to a polymer?
options: It creates strong cross-links that make the polymer completely rigid.
It causes the polymer to undergo a displacement reaction.
It gets between polymer molecules, allowing them to move over each other more easily.
It turns the synthetic polymer into a natural ceramic.

questions.question: How do cross-links between polymer molecules affect the properties of a polymer?
options: They make the polymer harder and less flexible.
They make the polymer much softer and highly soluble in water.
They lower the melting point so it melts at room temperature.
They allow the polymer molecules to slide past each other much more easily.

questions.question: When a reactive metal reacts with an acid, what are the products?
options: A metal oxide and water
A metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas
A metal salt and hydrogen gas.
A metal carbonate and oxygen gas

questions.question: What are the products when a reactive metal reacts with water?
options: A metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas.
A metal salt and carbon dioxide
A metal oxide and nitrogen gas
A metal sulfate and oxygen gas

questions.question: What does the reactivity series for metals show?
options: The different temperatures at which metals turn into ceramics.
How vigorously metals react compared to each other.
The exact number of monomers in a metal polymer.
How easily metals can be dissolved to make plasticisers.
